claim_scope: Original single Glossopteris browniana fossil-leaf surface-relief teaching specimen on a thin original solid sediment slab, informed by H.I.15 photo PlateIVe and original description in Kovacs-Endrody1976. No tree, whole organism, reproductive attachment, living leaf, exact specimen scan or measured fossil relief. Blade tongue-shaped with obtuse apex, narrowed base, prominent midrib and polygonal reticulate side venation. Nominal0.075x0.195x0.007m slab, approximately0.055x0.16m blade are illustrative. Shallow vein relief approximately0.15-0.25mm, no fossil-measured depth claim. Surface network is simplified original topology, not a traced scan. Bjuvia simplex comparison is an explicit conditional production gate, no pass asserted before actual neutral-control test.

source_references.notes: Keep concept entire tongue-shaped leaf and net connections; discard photoreal grain and broad modern-dicot hierarchical branches. Source browniana polygon meshes occur across blade, parallel median vein bundle visible as midrib. Use many closely spaced oblique side veins that bifurcate and reconnect with shorter bridges, not a few thick branching tree veins. Bound relief width/depth so it remains a thin fossil teaching prop, not rope venation. No living underside or attached seeds. Same outline, material, normalized size, light/camera and comparable vein prominence used for Bjuvia simplex parallel-veined diagnostic control. Control is non-delivery and not fifth asset; actual source photo, no blank-flat strawman. If net topology unreadable at512px without unsupported exaggeration, stop Glossopteris production rather than waive audit129.
